turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Mr. Reyes, thank you for coming in. Your pathology report is back, and I want to go over it and the next steps with you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Just tell me straight. Did they get it all?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The surgeon removed the tumor. Cancer cells were in 3 of the 14 lymph nodes, so this is stage three colon cancer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Stage three sounds really bad. Am I going to die from this?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: We recommend chemotherapy after surgery, called FOLFOX, every two weeks for about three to six months. It lowers the chance the cancer comes back. Common side effects are nausea, tiredness, and numbness or tingling in the hands and feet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Will I still be able to work? I drive a truck.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Before we plan, are you taking any blood thinners? And do you have any numbness in your feet now?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No blood thinners, just my blood pressure pill. And my feet are fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay. We plan to start in two weeks. You will come in every other week, we draw blood first, and a small pump goes home with you for two days. Then the nurse will go over the paperwork.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sorry, did you say a pump goes home with me? I didn’t catch the last part.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: The nurse will go over all of that. Any other questions?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: A nurse navigator named Maria will call you this week. We will see you in two weeks.
